statement: certificate existence is equivalent to the abc conjecture (honesty check)

premises.note: Certificate implies abc (Theorem 2, proved in cl03_implication.json)

proof_steps.label: forward-direction
proof_steps.justification: This is exactly CL-03 (Theorem 2). See cl03_implication.json.

proof_steps.label: converse-setup
proof_steps.claim: Assume abc conjecture holds. We construct a certificate.
proof_steps.justification: The converse uses abc as a HYPOTHESIS — this is permitted. The abc assumption is not a construction leaf. The [OBL] construction (M1/M2/M3) must not use abc; this converse proof lives in M6 where abc is a hypothesis.
proof_steps.note: The abc conjecture is used here as a hypothesis in the converse proof, not as a construction leaf (spec §2.3, B4).

proof_steps.label: converse-exception-set
proof_steps.claim: Assuming abc, the set E_eps = {(a,b,c) coprime, a+b=c : c > K_eps * rad(abc)^(1+eps)} is finite
proof_steps.justification: This is the definition of the abc conjecture: it asserts finitely many exceptions. Given abc, E_eps is finite by hypothesis.

proof_steps.label: converse-K_epsilon-construction
proof_steps.claim: Define K_eps = max_{(a,b,c) in E_eps} c / rad(abc)^(1+eps). This is a finite maximum over a finite set.
proof_steps.justification: The max over a finite set is well-defined. This K_eps is constructed from the hypothesis (abc), not from known abc triples used to fit K_eps. It is a proof-internal construction in the converse direction.
proof_steps.note: This construction is ONLY valid in the converse proof where abc is a hypothesis. The [OBL] construction in M2 must derive K_eps independently.

proof_steps.label: converse-certificate
proof_steps.claim: The tuple (eps, K_eps, trivial-P_height, P_ineq-from-abc, finiteness-from-step-3) is a valid certificate.
proof_steps.justification: Each component: P_height is trivially satisfied (the rad function is already defined via CL-01); P_ineq holds universally by abc hypothesis; P_finiteness holds by step 3.

proof_steps.label: biconditional
proof_steps.justification: Forward: step 1 (CL-03). Converse: steps 2-5 construct a certificate from the abc hypothesis.

proof_steps.label: honesty-implication
proof_steps.claim: The inequality alone (without a construction of K_eps from non-abc input) is NOT a shortcut to abc.
proof_steps.justification: The converse uses abc as a hypothesis to construct K_eps. Therefore, if the [OBL] construction derives K_eps from known abc triples or abc-equivalent assertions, it is circular and fails CORE-1 (forbidden construction leaves). The system is honest: the inequality alone has no more content than abc itself.
proof_steps.note: This is the honesty check of Theorem 3 (spec §2.3). It prevents the K_eps construction from being a trivial reformulation.

non_circularity: The forward direction (CL-03) uses no abc input. The converse uses abc as a hypothesis only — this is permitted and recorded explicitly. No construction in M1/M2/M3 uses abc.
